item.title: Spooky-Season Theatre to Chill You to the Bone
item.description: Also: the gorgeous new musical of “The Curious Case of Benjamin Button,” the sumptuous sound of Yebba, American Ballet Theatre’s fall season, and more.

item.title: Andre D. Wagner’s Eye for the Photo-Ready
item.description: Wagner knows the special alchemy that can happen when you point a camera at a Black person on the street.
item.dc:creator: ByHanif Abdurraqib

item.title: The Republicans’ Remarkably Bad Midterm Campaigns
item.description: Things were going poorly even before Vivek Ramaswamy’s campaign ran the most offensive ad of the year.
item.dc:creator: ByBenjamin Wallace-Wells

item.title: For Bob Iger, That’s the Way It Is
item.description: The former Ithaca weatherman became Disney’s C.E.O. Now he’s just like everyone else—retired and co-owning the Los Angeles Lakers with Josh Kushner, by way of Karlie Kloss.
item.dc:creator: ByBen McGrath

item.title: A Pickpocket’s Guide to New York
item.description: Preparing to play a petty thief in a new movie, John Turturro learned the moves—“reefing the kick” among them—from Apollo Robbins, and observed how much stealing has in common with acting.
item.dc:creator: ByMichael Schulman

item.title: Daniel Humm’s Home Décor
item.description: The Eleven Madison Park chef surveys his cozy new restaurant in the West Village with the artists who decked it out, Rashid Johnson and Francesco Clemente.
item.dc:creator: ByEmma Allen

item.title: From the Battalion to Broadway
item.description: Alex Ekker served four years in the Marine Corps—then decided to be an actor. While sightseeing at the Empire State Building, he talks about his professional début in Aaron Sorkin’s “A Few Good Men.”
item.dc:creator: BySarah Larson

item.title: Charles Kushner and the MAGA Ambassador’s Playbook
item.description: Since taking up his post in Paris, Kushner has become known for lobbing provocations onto France’s domestic scene at sensitive moments. As he put it, “Nobody has the courage to say what I say.”
item.dc:creator: ByLauren Collins

item.title: How Jim Morrison Surmounted Tragedy and Skied Down Everest
item.description: The mountaineer and his partner, Hilaree Nelson, planned a first-ever descent. After her death, he pushed on.
item.dc:creator: ByNick Paumgarten

item.title: The State Officials Defending the Midterms from the President
item.description: Donald Trump has tried to purge voter rolls nationwide. Deidre Henderson, the Republican lieutenant governor of Utah, is among the chief election officers standing in his way.
item.dc:creator: ByBarton Gellman

item.title: Did an Alternative-Medicine Guru Accidentally Kill Patients?
item.description: In Switzerland, Thomas Rau offers treatments that many conventional doctors would question. Now he’s accused of lethally negligent care.
item.dc:creator: ByD. T. Max

item.title: Cheeks
item.description: A young New Yorker considers moving away.
item.dc:creator: ByAdrian Tomine

item.title: “Wall Cano”
item.description: I didn’t know what homework was. And since my parents had never gone to school themselves, they never asked me about it.
item.dc:creator: BySouvankham Thammavongsa

item.title: The Gold Rush and the Making of Modern America
item.description: The best-selling author Nathaniel Philbrick sees links between eighteen-fifties California and the current A.I. boom. What can the history of the action-packed gold rush actually tell us?
item.dc:creator: ByKathryn Schulz

item.title: Briefly Noted
item.description: “Ausländer,” “Frivolity: A Defense,” “May We Feed the King,” and “Sophie, Standing There.”

item.title: Why the Broadway Musical Refuses to Die
item.description: Broadway once thrived on the collision of musical traditions. Now, amid jukebox shows and Hollywood adaptations, can it recover its creative daring?
item.dc:creator: ByAdam Gopnik

item.title: The Victoria & Albert Museum Expands, Twice
item.description: Two new outposts of the London institution make a vibrant case for handmade craft in an age of A.I. slop.
item.dc:creator: ByRebecca Mead

item.title: Political Skirmishes in “Other Desert Cities” and “A Bright Room Called Day”
item.description: Revivals of plays by Jon Robin Baitz and Tony Kushner.

item.title: The Fragile Unions of “Possible Love”
item.description: In Lee Chang-dong’s brilliantly acted film, a community’s devastation plays out through a documentary lens—and through a tale of two very different couples.
item.dc:creator: ByJustin Chang

item.title: Waves, Cords

item.dc:creator: ByAlfred Corn
